contract: Evaluate one pure Lua function of one plain input in a fresh PUC Lua 5.4.9 process outside the VM, over a caller-held OTP Port with length-framed JSON, under policy version 1 (a fixed helper-free allow-list) and exact positive limits on counted steps, call depth, value bytes, live Lua memory and wall time; a refusal is a fixed atom, memory, wall time, abnormal exit and protocol failure are host outcomes, and the child is reaped on every return path.
limits: Not OS security isolation: no container, seccomp, namespace, network or filesystem confinement; Port separation does not protect against a native-runtime vulnerability. Policy version 1 grants no helpers, bindings, callbacks, clocks, random or I/O.

The string guard reads the private TString layout and allocation tag of the pinned Lua checkout; the build verifies the exact upstream bytes and a different revision is refused, but the coupling must be re-audited with each upstream change.

Memory, wall time and abnormal exit depend on allocator timing, scheduling and the operating system, so they are recorded outcomes and never replay decisions; no cross-build replay claim: operators keep the pinned runtime's semantics.
A fresh empty object cannot be built by a version 1 source; a decoded empty object round-trips. Tables made by table.pack carry an n key and are not dense arrays.

grounding.claim: Fresh build from the installed pinned checkout, 42 from a pure function, missing compiler and archiver, wrong revision, extra header and failed compile refuse, no write into the source checkout; listed scenarios pass.

Plain-data round trips, bounds at the cap and cap + 1, malformed frames driven by fake executables, child crash and stderr text, and one smoke scenario for each limit mechanism; listed scenarios pass.
Policy identity is canonical and the audit of the fresh environment equals the descriptor; listed scenarios pass.
Relies on the pinned Lua 5.4.9 checkout: the public C API, the count/call/return hooks, lua_Alloc and the private TString layout; the build verifies the exact bytes.
Relies on Port semantics: spawn_executable, exit_status, environment unset, and exit reports after the child is reaped.
Relies on Jason 1.4.5 strict decoding with ordered objects so duplicate keys are detected.

cc, ar and kill exist on the host; the OS delivers SIGKILL to the child; the compiler honors the fixed defines; policy-only sources behave identically across fresh processes of one build (part of the later replay group).

telemetry.contract: No event, log or measurement is emitted and no observation payload exists; nothing carries source, input or result outside the return value.

config.contract: Limits are exact per-request operands and the policy is fixed by its identity; there is no ambient or hot Config.

control.contract: No independent Control API: a run ends by its own limits or by the caller's deadline, and the caller-held Port reaps the child.
